page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highcpu-16 is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9B45 processor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The system is equipped with 30.0 GB of RAM, providing a resource density of 1.88 GB per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU accelerators, and comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU testing and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression scoring in the top 10% of tested systems. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores, falls within the average range. Memory bandwidth is moderate, measuring 53.46 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 34.08 GB/sec for large-block write operations. Small-model LLM inference is highly efficient, achieving top-tier text generation speeds of 424.39 tokens/sec for a 135M parameter model.

The server's low memory-to-vCPU ratio represents a clear tradeoff, prioritizing raw compute power over memory capacity. This configuration is highly cost-efficient for compute-bound tasks that do not require massive memory footprints or local disk storage. It is well-suited for workloads such as single-threaded data processing, lightweight LLM inference, web serving, and general-purpose compute tasks that benefit from strong single-core CPU execution.
